15.title: 3Sum
15.insight: Reduces 3Sum to repeated 2Sum on sorted subarrays. Duplicate skipping is what makes it clean.

128.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
128.insight: Only start counting from sequence beginnings. Skipping elements that are mid-sequence avoids revisiting.

238.title: Product of Array Except Self
238.insight: Each element = product of everything left × everything right. Two independent passes, no division needed.

200.title: Number of Islands
200.insight: Must track which prefixes are valid, not just look up substrings.

152.title: Maximum Product Subarray
152.insight: Negative × negative = positive. Track both extremes at each position.

5.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
5.insight: Rotation guarantees one half is always sorted. Use that to decide which half to discard.

73.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
73.insight: First row/column can double as marker storage. Process markers last to avoid overwriting.

11.title: Container With Most Water
11.insight: The shorter line limits the area. Moving the taller line inward can only decrease width without increasing height.

207.title: Course Schedule
207.insight: BFS alone can't detect cycles. In-degree tracking ensures prerequisites are satisfied before visiting.

146.title: LRU Cache
146.insight: Doubly linked list allows O(1) removal from middle. Stack can't do that.

102.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
102.insight: Queue size at each iteration = number of nodes at that level.

322.title: Coin Change
322.insight: Each amount depends on smaller amounts. Build up, don't recurse down.

98.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
98.insight: In-order of BST is strictly increasing. One pass, one check.

133.title: Clone Graph
133.insight: Map prevents infinite loops on cycles. Clone on first visit, reuse on revisit.

153.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
153.insight: One comparison with right boundary is enough to decide which half to keep.

416.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
416.insight: Partition equal sum = subset sum to total/2. One boolean array, iterate backwards to avoid reuse.

236.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of Binary Tree
236.insight: LCA is the first node where p and q diverge into different subtrees. Recursion naturally finds it.

19.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
19.insight: One pass with two pointers spaced n apart. No need to compute list length.

3.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
3.insight: Map stores last seen index of each character. Jump left directly past the duplicate, no incremental shrink.

208.title: Implement Trie
208.insight: Fixed-width array at each node gives O(1) child lookup. isEnd distinguishes prefixes from complete words.

76.title: Minimum Window Substring
76.insight: Track required vs available counts. Shrink while all requirements met, expand when broken.

148.title: Sort List
148.insight: Merge sort is the natural fit for linked lists — split is O(1) with fast/slow pointers, merge is O(n) with dummy head.

1481.title: Least Number of Unique Integers after K Removals
1481.insight: Reuse means recursion tree depth isn't bounded by array length. Prune when current sum exceeds target.

48.title: Rotate Image
48.insight: Rotate = transpose + reverse. Two simple ops instead of tracking four-way swaps.

84.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
84.insight: Each popped index defines a rectangle that extends left (previous smaller) and right (current smaller). The stack maintains "next smaller to the left" — when it breaks, you know the rectangle's boundaries.

56.title: Merge Intervals
56.insight: Sorting guarantees you only need to look at the previous interval — no backtracking needed. Merge or push, never skip.

31.title: Next Permutation
31.insight: Backtracking gives all permutations in O(n!) — overkill. One linear scan + one swap + one reverse gives the next permutation directly.

394.title: Decode String
394.insight: `[` saves state (current string and repeat count) to stacks, `]` restores and applies. Same idea as recursion but explicit.

49.title: Group Anagrams
49.insight: Your approach works but is O(n²) because you compare every pair. Sorting or counting as the key groups in one pass — no pairwise comparison needed.

155.title: Min Stack
155.insight: Your linked list idea works too — essentially the same thing. Min stack approach is cleaner to implement. The ≤ on push (not <) handles duplicates correctly.

287.title: Find the Duplicate Number
287.insight: No extra structure needed — indices ARE your pointers. In-place, O(1) space.

54.title: Spiral Matrix
54.insight: Each traversal shrinks the "ring" — boundaries are your state, not recursion.

78.title: Subsets
78.insight: Same as combo/permutation backtracking — just don't track a target. Every node in the tree is a valid subset.

46.title: Permutations
46.insight: Two clean implementations — swap-in-place or build-new-list. Both give the same result. Swap-in-place is O(1) space, build-new-list is cleaner to reason about.

104.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
104.insight: In-order isn't required — any traversal works. DFS is simplest: base case is null (return 0), otherwise 1 + max of children.

136.title: Single Number
136.insight: XOR is its own inverse. a ^ a = 0, a ^ 0 = a. Order doesn't matter.

2.title: Add Two Numbers
2.insight: Reverse order is a gift — you process least significant digit first, which is exactly what addition needs.

198.title: House Robber
198.insight: You only need the last two states. Not prefix sums — it's a decision at each step, not a guaranteed include.

300.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
300.insight: Your state description is correct — that's the O(n²) DP. The O(n log n) optimization uses binary search on tails instead of scanning all previous elements.

141.title: Linked List Cycle
141.insight: In a cycle, fast gains 1 step per iteration on slow. It's guaranteed to lap slow within one cycle length.

560.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
560.insight: Combo recursion is O(2^n). Prefix sum reduces it to one pass — each position asks "have I seen the sum that makes this subarray equal k?"

494.title: Target Sum
494.insight: Assigning +/- is the same as picking a "positive" subset. Reframing as subset sum reduces exponential to O(n × sum). **FLAG: Review before interview — user wants to revisit.**

1091.title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
1091.insight: BFS explores level by level — the first time you reach the destination is guaranteed shortest. DFS doesn't have that guarantee.

981.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
981.insight: Each key's values are naturally inserted in timestamp order, so the list is already sorted. Binary search is the right tool for "largest ≤ target."

116.title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node
116.insight: Perfect binary tree means the next pointers you've already set give you a free linked list to traverse when setting up the next level.

347.title: Top K Frequent Elements
347.insight: Bucket sort avoids O(n log n) sorting. Frequency is bounded by n, so you get O(n) guaranteed.

994.title: Rotting Oranges
994.insight: The O(m×n) scan at the end is unnecessary — just track the fresh count as you go. When BFS finishes, one comparison tells you if it's possible.

230.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
230.insight: In-order of BST is sorted. You don't need to traverse the whole tree — stop as soon as k hits 0.

105.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
105.insight: Preorder gives you the root. Inorder tells you the size of left/right subtrees. Use the left subtree size to split the preorder array correctly.

55.title: Jump Game
55.insight: You don't need to track which path — just track the farthest you can possibly reach. If every index up to the end is reachable, you're good.

75.title: Sort Colors
75.insight: Three-way partition in a single pass. Mid walks forward, low and high converge from ends.

210.title: Course Schedule II
210.insight: Regular BFS with a visited set can revisit nodes. In-degree tracking ensures you only visit each node once prerequisites are satisfied.

62.title: Unique Paths
62.insight: Recursion + memoization works but bottom-up avoids stack overhead. 1D compression works because each cell only depends on top and left.

131.title: Palindrome Partitioning
131.insight: Same tree structure as subsets/combo — just with a palindrome check as the gate for valid branches.

199.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
199.insight: Just following right children misses nodes in left subtree when right subtree is shorter. Track depth to capture deeper visible nodes.

235.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
235.insight: BST ordering means you don't need to search both subtrees — one comparison tells you which direction to go. No need to check for nulls.

79.title: Word Search
79.insight: The exponential factor is 4^L not 4^(m×n) because you stop at word length. Unmarking (backtracking) is what allows revisiting cells on different paths.

221.title: Maximal Square
221.insight: A square at (i,j) can only exist if there are squares above, left, and diagonally above-left. The minimum of those three + 1 gives the largest square ending here. Use bottom-up 1D DP to avoid stack overflow.

91.title: Decode Ways
91.insight: Backtracking is exponential. DP with two states back is O(n) — at each position you have at most two choices (1 digit or 2 digits), and you only need the next two values.

437.title: Path Sum III
437.insight: Same idea as LC560 (Subarray Sum Equals K) — but on a tree. The map tracks prefix sums along the current path. Backtracking the map when you leave a node ensures you only count paths in the current branch.

1029.title: Two City Scheduling
1029.insight: The person with the biggest savings going to A (vs B) should go to A. Sort by difference, take top n for A.

138.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
138.insight: Map eliminates the need to search for random targets. Two passes — one to build nodes, one to wire pointers.

1143.title: Longest Common Subsequence
1143.insight: Backtracking over all shared chars is exponential. DP with two indices is O(m×n) — at each position, you either match or skip one char from either string.

739.title: Daily Temperatures
739.insight: Same idea as LC84 — stack maintains "next greater element" to the right. When you find one, compute the distance and pop.

100.title: Same Tree
100.insight: Order doesn't matter as long as both trees use the same traversal. Pre-order is simplest — check current, then recurse left and right.

121.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
121.insight: You only need to know the cheapest price you've seen up to now. One pass, two variables.

463.title: Island Perimeter
463.insight: 4 minus number of adjacent land cells, summed over all land cells.

226.title: Invert Binary Tree
226.insight: Post-order works naturally — children are inverted before you swap them. Pre-order also works (swap then recurse). Either way, every node gets exactly one swap.

1024.title: Video Stitching
1024.insight: No backtracking needed — pure greedy. Extending coverage as far as possible at each step is always optimal. Picking shorter leaves less room for future clips.

1249.title: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
1249.insight: You only need to track ( positions — unmatched ) are simply ignored during the scan. Stack tells you which ( to remove at the end.

1539.title: Kth Missing Positive Number
1539.insight: Gap-walking is O(n). Binary search on the missing count formula gives O(log n). Missing before arr[i] = arr[i] - (i + 1).

334.title: Increasing Triplet Subsequence
334.insight: second and first don't need to come from the same subsequence — second being updated means a smaller element existed before it. So finding anything > second always yields a valid triplet.

1423.title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
1423.insight: Taking i from left and k-i from right = skipping a contiguous block of n-k. Sliding that block left to right explores all valid splits in one pass.

438.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
438.insight: Window always slides by one — never skips. But chars not in p act as blockers that keep matches < 26 until they slide out. The `matches` counter makes each step O(1) instead of O(26).

735.title: Asteroid Collision
735.insight: The while loop is the tricky part — after popping a smaller positive, the incoming negative might still collide with the next positive on the stack. Each asteroid pushed/popped at most once.

64.title: Minimum Path Sum
64.insight: DFS is O(2^(m+n)) without memo. DP with 1D compression — each cell depends only on cell above and cell to the left, update in place left to right, top to bottom.

1048.title: Longest String Chain
1048.insight: Predecessor = remove exactly one character to get the other word. Frequency map check doesn't work — "ab" and "ba" have same frequencies but neither is a predecessor. Removing one char at a time and checking existence is the correct test.

1347.title: Minimum Number of Steps to Make Two Strings Anagram
1347.insight: Two strings of equal length are anagrams iff their frequency maps are identical. Count the gap between maps — that's the answer.

380.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
380.insight: Swap-and-pop keeps the array dense — no tombstones, no gaps to track. Remove is O(1) because the map always has correct indices after the swap.

567.title: Permutation in String
567.insight: Same problem as LC438 — just return true/false instead of all start indices.

904.title: Fruit Into Baskets
904.insight: "Two baskets" = at most 2 distinct values in the window. Classic variable-size sliding window — expand until constraint breaks, shrink to restore.

71.title: Simplify Path
71.insight: Each component is independent — just push, pop, or skip. No counting or running string needed. Join at the end.

424.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
424.insight: Replacements needed = window_size - most_frequent_count. Keep expanding while that's ≤ k. max_freq is monotonically non-decreasing — no need to shrink it.

1300.title: Sum of Mutated Array Closest to Target
1300.insight: After sorting, each candidate value replaces all elements >= it with itself. Prefix sums let you compute the resulting sum in O(1) per candidate.

309.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
309.insight: Cooldown is captured by the state machine — after selling, you must pass through rest before buying again. Three states keep the transitions clean.

24.title: Swap Nodes in Pairs
24.insight: Dummy head eliminates edge cases for head swaps. Each pair swap is the same four pointer reassignments — prev always anchors the operation.

176.title: Second Highest Salary
176.insight: LIMIT/OFFSET is close but needs DISTINCT for duplicates. Subquery version is cleaner — find max, then find max below it.

47.title: Permutations II
47.insight: Same as LC46 but with duplicate handling. Sort + "previous not used at this level" check eliminates duplicate permutations without needing a set per recursion level.

1177.title: Can Make Palindrome from Substring
1177.insight: In a palindrome, at most one character has odd frequency. Each change fixes two odd counts, so odd_count / 2 is minimum changes needed. Prefix sums make substring frequency queries O(26).

515.title: Find Largest Value in Each Tree Row
515.insight: Queue size at each iteration = number of nodes at that level. Track max per level, reset for next.

318.title: Maximum Product of Word Lengths
318.insight: Bitmask AND is O(1) vs O(26) for freq map intersection. Same complexity, better constant factor.

725.title: Split Linked List in Parts
725.insight: Simple division math — extra nodes distributed one each to the first extra parts. Walk once, split at computed sizes.

1701.title: Average Waiting Time
1701.insight: Customer waits if chef is still busy (finish > arrival). Otherwise starts immediately. Greedy — serve in order, carry finish time forward.

1823.title: Find the Winner of the Circular Game
1823.insight: No array needed. Each iteration computes the survivor's position in a circle of size i from the winner in size i-1. Elimination offset is always k.

274.title: H-Index
274.insight: Unlike sorting (O(n log n)), bucket sort exploits the fact that citations are bounded by n. Capping at n is the trick — h can't exceed the number of papers.

1658.title: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
1658.insight: Removing from ends = keeping a contiguous middle. Minimize removals = maximize kept subarray. Positivity guarantees monotonic sum — right advances when sum < target, left advances when sum > target, record when sum == target. Each element added once (right passes it) and removed at most once (left passes it) — 2n total moves, amortized O(n).

478.title: Generate Random Point in a Circle
478.insight: Area scales with r², so radius density must be proportional to r (not uniform). √(uniform) transforms uniform U[0,1] via inverse CDF of F(r) = r²/R². Rejection sampling also works: proposal = uniform over bounding square [−R,R]², target = uniform over circle. c = sup target(x)/proposal(x) = (1/πR²)/(1/4R²) = 4/π ≈ 1.273. Accept ratio = 1/c ≈ 78.5% = area of circle / area of square.

3531.title: Count Covered Buildings
3531.insight:
"Four directions" decomposes into independent row and column existence checks. Binary search in sorted groups determines whether neighbors exist on both sides.
```
rows = { 1→[2], 2→[1,2,3], 3→[2] }
cols = { 1→[2], 2→[1,2,3], 3→[2] }
(2,2): rows[2] idx=1 → left(1) right(3) ✓, cols[2] idx=1 → above(1) below(3) ✓ → covered
(1,2): rows[1] len=1 → no horizontal neighbors ✗ → not covered
```

3796.title: Find Maximum Value in a Constrained Sequence ⚑ REVISIT
3796.pattern: Constraint Propagation / Shortest Path on Line
3796.insight: |a[i]-a[i+1]| ≤ diff[i] gives two directed inequalities. Chain is a DAG — forward pass propagates left-to-right increases, backward pass propagates right-to-left decreases from restrictions. The tightest bound is the intersection of both passes.

3546.title: Equal Sum Grid Partition I
3546.insight: Single prefix check works for each direction — no need for both forward and backward. If total is odd, impossible immediately.

16.title: 3Sum Closest
16.insight: Same skeleton as 3Sum but replace "sum == 0" with "track min absolute difference." Two-pointer direction always moves sum toward target.

3377.title: Digit Operations to Make Two Integers Equal
3377.insight: Edge weights depend on target node (not source), so Dijkstra still works — cost accumulates additively. Prime constraint makes greedy fail; graph is small enough for full search.

848.title: Shifting Letters
848.insight: Naively applying each shift to i+1 letters is O(n²). Each letter's total shift = sum of shifts[i..n-1] — one pass from right.

319.title: Bulb Switcher
319.insight: Divisors come in pairs unless i is a perfect square. Only perfect-square bulbs are toggled an odd number of times → left on.

2592.title: Maximize Greatness of an Array
2592.insight: Pair smallest beater with smallest target — never waste a large element. Greedy on sorted arrays is optimal because ordering preserves the "greater than" relation transitively.

1438.title: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff ≤ Limit
1438.insight: Two deques maintain running min and max in O(1) amortized per operation. Condition is any two elements, so both min and max must be tracked.

621.title: Task Scheduler
621.insight: Cycle detection in undirected graph reduces to checking if endpoints are already connected before adding edge. First edge where find(u)==find(v) is the redundant one.

167.title: Two Sum II (Input Array Is Sorted)
167.insight: Sorted input enables linear two-pointer instead of hash map. The monotonicity of sum with respect to pointer movement guarantees finding the pair.

875.title: Koko Eating Bananas
875.insight: Feasibility function is monotonic — if k works, any k' > k also works. Binary search on the threshold.

2029.title: Stone Game IX
2029.insight: Only mod-3 classes matter, not actual values. Game reduces to counting remainders and reasoning about forced sequences.

3255.title: Find the Power of K-Size Subarrays II
3255.insight: "Consecutive ascending" means +1 exactly, not monotonic. Valid window's max is its last element. Single pass with running counter — no stack needed.

1404.title: Number of Steps to Reduce a Number in Binary Representation to One
1404.insight: No conversion to int — binary string is already the number. Operations map directly to string manipulation: divide = drop LSB, subtract = flip LSB 1→0 (with carry propagation). Carry tracks pending subtraction across bits.

1915.title: Number of Wonderful Substrings
1915.pattern: Bit Manipulation / Prefix XOR / Hash Map
1915.insight: Parity is the only thing that matters for "at most one odd" condition. XOR tracks parity toggles. Wonderful = mask has 0 or 1 set bits. 10 letters max enables O(10) per position.
